blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: accelerator — Hardware specialised for particular workloads.
throughput — Amount of work per unit time.

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.text: RISC/CISC and CPU/GPU are not a single four-way classification: a processor's ISA, core organisation and accelerators are different design properties.

blocks.title: Apply
blocks.text: A graphics or machine-learning workload with abundant parallel operations may benefit from a GPU; sequential/control-intensive jobs suit general CPU cores.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Choose based on power, energy budget, latency, software compatibility, transfer overhead and ability to divide the workload; support claims with mechanism.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the choice
blocks.text: A low-power embedded CPU (often using a RISC architecture) is reasonable; no large GPU is needed for tiny sequential work.

questions.feedback: accelerator — Hardware specialised for particular workloads.

blocks.title: Explain the choice
blocks.text: A GPU can accelerate similar independent pixel/shading operations, paired with a CPU for control.
